Description:
A hush falls over the bustling city square as a fat pig adorned in a lavish display of gold and diamonds walks around the corner, accompanied by a pair of brutish lackeys, oblivious to the imminent danger lurking in the shadows. concealed within his pocket rests a scroll containing privileged information for his eyes only, or so he believes. Now! A shadowy figure descends upon them, a poisoned blade finding its mark in the unsuspecting guard's back. Swift and precise strikes to the legs, a tap on the shoulder and a trick of the shadows renders the swine isolated in the dim alley. Flee, little pig, and squal in vain - your cries fall upon deaf ears.
It is finished. A message stolen, and one conveyed. From whom? That is for the little pig and his friends to determine. After all, it was the quickest way for him to lose weight; he'll have an easier time trotting home.
Rogues are masters of the shadows who focus on subtlety, teamwork or direct combat. While they don't directly cast magic, they can train in the strange arts of shadow techniques - scholars debate wether this is a form of the arcane, psionics or a mere trick of the light. Only rogues know.
Quick Note: Rogues are masters of the shadows who focus on subtlety, teamwork or direct combat. While they don't directly cast magic, they can train in the strange arts of shadow techniques - scholars debate wether this is a form of the arcane, psionics or a mere trick of the light. Only rogues know.
Weapons: You are Trained in 2 Weapon Categories of choice (e.g. One-Handed Melee, Two-Handed Ranged, Shields, etc).
Language: You know Doublespeak! Doublespeak is not exactly a language, but a way to carry out private conversations in public by using code words and phrases with double meaning, such that what you say is indistinguishable from a normal conversation. Doublespeak also has a written version; thieves, rogues and streetspeople might use deliberate writing mistakes, punctuation errors or scratch marks on buildings to warn or convey concepts or even entire sentences; these markings are indistinguishable from random scratches to the unaware. Doublespeak is an art in itself - even if every doublespeaker has their own mannerisms and idiosyncracies, one must know and recognize the patterns to be able to speak this language properly, and as such, some even consider it a poetic "language".

Spellcasting.Text: Unlike other Classes, you do not use Mana, and can't normally spend it on Abilities. You rely solely on your own Class Abilities and Talents, which are often stronger than usual and may provide more interesting options.
Spellcasting.Change: You can change your known Spells and Talents inbetween Adventures.
Spellcasting.Other: All Rogue-specific Abilities are not considered Spells (unless stated otherwise).
Spellcasting.Recommended Abilities Description: Shank is there to help you spend your Mana in uncanny situations where you need just a little more damage to finish of an enemy. In case of an emergency, Recuperate is there to Heal you, while Slam will deal Mass Damage in case you're fighting multiple enemies. Finally, if you find out your enemies are resistant to your weapon attacks, get Lightstrike. It's situational, but it can be effective!

~Hamorrhage~.Effect:
This Turn, you deal -100% Damage.
However, all Damage you would have done is instead applied to the enemy as a delayed _wound_.
The next time it takes Damage, it also takes all the _wound_ Damage.
~Hamorrhage~.Name: ~Hamorrhage~

~Dust of Appearance~.Effect:
Mark a Unit with _dust of appearance_.
Other allies deal +10% Damage with all attacks against the marked Unit.
~Dust of Appearance~.Name: ~Dust of Appearance~

~Hidden in Plain Sight~.Effect: In the first round of every combat, enemies can't target you with attacks or Abilities.
~Hidden in Plain Sight~.Name: ~Hidden in Plain Sight~

Starting Abilities Description.Ambush:
Ambush can normally happen only once per turn, and you can charge it up to deal more Damage!
However, your Rogue Specialization will give you extra ways to Ambush target!

Starting Abilities Description.Stalking: Essentially, you can interrupt another Unit's turn, put that unit on pause, and start your turn. When your turn ends, the Unit resumes its turn.

~Ambush~.Effect: Every Worthy Combat, your first weapon attack deals +1d8 Damage.
~Ambush~.Upgrade: At Level 2, your Specialization will greatly improve your Ambush.
~Ambush~.Name: ~Ambush~

~Stalking~.Effect: On the first Round of Combat, you can start your Turn whenever you like (even during other Units' turns), and make a free Move Act.
~Stalking~.Upgrade: You do count as a Hero Turn towards monsters' Setback, and so perhaps more monsters will take their Turn after you.
~Stalking~.Notes:
If you interrupted an Ally's Turn, monsters may take their Turn immediately after you if their Setback is enough. Then the Ally can resume their Turn.
If you want to start during an enemy's Turn, you do so when they declare they want to do something or after they finish doing something.
~Stalking~.Name: ~Stalking~

~Bells and Whistles~.Effect:
You setup an invisible 6x6x6 meter area.
If an unknown Unit or Enemy enters the cube, you are immediately alerted and woken up.
While inside the area, ^you^ cannot be Surprised.
~Bells and Whistles~.Name: ~Bells and Whistles~

~Camping~.Effect:
Setup camp, creating favorable conditions for your party for up to 8 in-game hours.
Units in the camp are protected from all bad weather and are immune to being poisoned by food and drink.
Until the end of the Adventure, all Units who camped here are immune to Hard Terrain.
~Camping~.Name: ~Camping~
~Camping~.Notes: Moving 1 meter through Hard Terrain takes 2 meters of Movement.

~Panther's Paw~.Effect: You are immune to Fall Damage.
~Panther's Paw~.Name: ~Panther's Paw~

~Fame and Fortune~.Effect: The next time you deal Damage, gain {Gold}Gold equal to 300% of the Damage dealt.
~Fame and Fortune~.Name: ~Fame and Fortune~

~Knife Throw~.Effect: Your next melee One-Handed weapon attack has a 4 meter range.
~Knife Throw~.Name: ~Knife Throw~

~Parry~.Effect: Your next attack deals -50% Damage, but gives an ally you can see one Shielding that can block 1d6 Damage.
~Parry~.Name: ~Parry~

<Pocket Sand>.Name: <Pocket Sand>
<Pocket Sand>.Notes: A Blind Unit's next Damage/Heal Act deals -50% Damage/Healing.

~Goldborn~.Effect: You can spend 300 {Gold}Gold to gain +2 Maximum Health, up to +10 total.
~Goldborn~.Name: ~Goldborn~

~Doublesault~.Effect: Leap up to 3 meters. If you land on a Unit, Doublesault again (for free)!
~Doublesault~.Notes:
You leap from Unit to Unit until you no longer land on a Unit. If you land on a Unit, you must leap again. You can't leap on the same Unit twice; if you do, you end your leap in the closest space near it.
You can use this even while in the air and it cancels out your current fall or acceleration.
~Doublesault~.Name: ~Doublesault~

~Creeping Ambush~.Effect: Insted of dealing Damage to the same target with Ambush, you can deal it to another Unit you can see.
~Creeping Ambush~.Name: ~Creeping Ambush~

~Lockpicking~.Effect: While you have this Talent, you have the Lockpicking Skill, and an extra +1 in Lockpicking.
~Lockpicking~.Name: ~Lockpicking~

~Gladiator Grandeur~.Effect:
Choose a Worthy Enemy.
Gain {Gold}Gold equal to the enemy's current Health.
That Enemy gains +1 {A}Action Point on its next Turn.
~Gladiator Grandeur~.Upgrade: You only gain 50% of an Epic Unit's current Health.
~Gladiator Grandeur~.Name: ~Gladiator Grandeur~

~Hemorrhage~.Effect:
Use after dealing Damage. Deal -100% Damage. However, all Damage you would have done instead becomes a delayed _wound_ on the target.
The next time it takes (more than 0) Damage, it consumes all _wounds_ and takes extra Damage equal to all the _wounds_.
~Hemorrhage~.Notes: Wounds add up until consumed. The Damager is considered the source of the wound Damage.
~Hemorrhage~.Name: ~Hemorrhage~

Specializations.Description:
At Level 1, you can choose your specialization.
Every Rogue can choose from the following Rogue specializations
Choices: Thief, an agile-handed individual, crafty and stealthy, dexterous and silent
Assassin, a person specialized in taking targets out one-on-one, through whatever means
Swashbuckler, an outlaw who is not afraid to engage in direct combat and apply whatever tricks necessary to get the job done

~Fool's Gold~.Effect: After you Ambush, gain {Gold}Gold equal to all the Damage done by the attack.
~Fool's Gold~.Notes: Lore-wise, as a Thief, you prepare and build up momentum in combat. When you reach a town, you put your preparations in motion and gain the gold. Feel free to them
~Fool's Gold~.Name: ~Fool's Gold~

~Ambush Upgrade~.Effect: Immediately pick a Level 2 Talent, which upgrades and replaces your starting Ambush.
~Ambush Upgrade~.Name: ~Ambush Upgrade~

~Backstabbing Ambush~.Effect: Every ~Turn~, your first weapon attack deals +1d6 Damage ~if there is an ally of yours near the target~.
~Backstabbing Ambush~.Name: ~Backstabbing Ambush~

~Icebreaker Ambush~.Effect: Every ~Turn~, your first weapon attack deals +1d10 Damage ~if the target is at full Health~.
~Icebreaker Ambush~.Name: ~Icebreaker Ambush~

~Thief's Ambush~.Effect:
Every Worthy Combat, your first weapon attack deals ~+2d8~ Damage ~and applies a ~Combo~~.
~Gain~ {Gold}~{Gold}Gold equal to the ambushed amount.~
~Thief's Ambush~.Name: ~Thief's Ambush~

<Magic Trickster>.Effect:
You have 2 {Mana}Mana that replenishes inbetween Adventures and gain access to one `Magic Font$/Other/MagicFonts` of choice.
When you get this Talent, you can pick 2 Magic Font Spells to Know.
<Magic Trickster>.Notes: You can change all these choices inbetween Adventures.
<Magic Trickster>.Name: <Magic Trickster>

<Verge of the Coin>.Effect: Whenever ^you^ would Damage a Worthy Enemy leaving it at 10% or less Health, it dies, and you gain {Gold}Gold equal to its Maximum Health.
<Verge of the Coin>.Name: <Verge of the Coin>

~Shade Bend~.Effect:
Choose a shadow you can see.
You can extend it upward to attack for 1d6 and Daze the target, or you can manipulate and control the shape of this shadow for up to 1 minute.
~Shade Bend~.Notes: This attack is able to trigger Ambush.
~Shade Bend~.Name: ~Shade Bend~

~Ghost Strike~.Effect: When you Ambush, also deal 50% of the Ambush Damage to another Unit within 3 meters of the main target.
~Ghost Strike~.Notes: Refers, for example, to the extra 1d8, not the entire attack's Damage.
~Ghost Strike~.Name: ~Ghost Strike~

<Hide In Plain Sight>.Effect:
When Combat starts, you can start on any visible edge of the battlefield.
The first time you deal Damage each Combat, you can choose to reroll any of the rolled dice.
<Hide In Plain Sight>.Notes: You know the ins and outs of battlefields so well that you successfully reposition before anyone else notices.
<Hide In Plain Sight>.Name: <Hide In Plain Sight>

<Bounty Appraisal>.Effect:
When Worthy Combat starts, the Quest Master determines which is the most powerful enemy.
When that enemy dies, Heal an ally for 1d10 and gain {Gold}Gold equal to 1000% of the amount healed.
<Bounty Appraisal>.Name: <Bounty Appraisal>

~Poison Craft~.Effect:
You coat each of your weapons in a potent poison.
Choose an effect for each.

Values: +1 Damage against Units with 25% or less Health
First attack with the weapon each Combat Slows the target
Weapon's Damage Type becomes Poison, Acid, or Scourge

~Poison Craft~.Name: ~Poison Craft~

<Magestep>.Effect:
Teleport up to 3 meters away.
Your next attack applies your Ambush if it wouldn't normally, and all the Damage becomes Fire, Cold or Shock (your choice).
<Magestep>.Downside: Ambush can only trigger Once / Turn.
<Magestep>.Name: <Magestep>

<Moneycraft>.Effect: Spend 400 {Gold}Gold to permanently improve a piece of equipment. Depending on its type (armor or weapon), roll on the table below to determine the effect you get.
<Moneycraft>.Upgrade: A piece of equipment can be improved any number of times, but every extra improvement costs twice as much as its previous improvement.
<Moneycraft>.Name: <Moneycraft>

<Trap Wires>.Effect:
When combat starts, deploy a number of Trap Wires equal to ^your Focus or Presence^, anywhere on the battlefield.
A Trap Wire is thin and up to 3 meters long, and must be deployed between 2 obstacles.
If a Unit touches a Trap Wire, it takes 1d10 Shock damage and becomes Dazed.
<Trap Wires>.Upgrade: Units with less than 2 Presence can't see the Trap Wires.
<Trap Wires>.Notes:
Each end of the wire must be attached to something solid and static.
You can make use of walls, obstacles, etc.
Requires a Special Tripwire Set item, which can be bought for 100 gold (or freely crafted for the same price in materials).
<Trap Wires>.Name: <Trap Wires>

<Blade Tempest>.Effect:
Throw 8 shurikens: one towards each direction (north, north-east, east, etc).
Each shuriken travels 4 meters, deals 2d6 Slash Damage to all Units it passes through, then stops in place.
At the end of your next turn, each shuriken returns to you, dealing 2d6 Slash Damage again to all Units it passes through.
<Blade Tempest>.Notes: Requires 8 Special Shuriken items, which can be bought for a total of 120 gold (or freely crafted for the same price in materials). If you're playing on a Grid, take semi-hitting into account for blades that don't travel squares exactly in the 8 directions. Cover applies normally to each blade.
<Blade Tempest>.Name: <Blade Tempest>

~Highway Robbery~.Effect: At the start of each Combat, choose a monster. All Units with the same name get +1 Setback. You gain +0.5 Initiative this Combat for each (up to +3).
~Highway Robbery~.Name: ~Highway Robbery~

<Gold Hoard>.Effect:
You gain various bonuses based on how much gold you are carrying.
You gain 1000% inventory capacity.

Values: +10% gold that ^you^ find and get from Abilities

<Gold Hoard>.Name: <Gold Hoard>

<Finders Keepers>.Effect: When looting a _lootable object_ that _contains Worthy items_, you can spend any amount of gold to also loot an item worth up to twice the spent amount.
<Finders Keepers>.Notes: It is up to the Quest Master what a _lootable object_ is (could be a chest, the corpse of an enemy, etc). Also, it is up to the Quest Master what _Worthy items_ means (could be main quest items, magic items, or just a normal chest).
<Finders Keepers>.Name: <Finders Keepers>

<Draw Steel>.Effect: Refresh all your other Cooldowns, Ambushes, and retrigger any _start of Combat_ effects from your Abilities.
<Draw Steel>.Notes: Refreshing an Ambush means you can use it again this Turn if you already used it.
<Draw Steel>.Name: <Draw Steel>

<Minor Golden Ambush>.Effect: When you Ambush, spend 10% of your carried total {Gold}Gold (minimum 100) to add +1d8 Damage.
<Minor Golden Ambush>.Notes: You need to have this gold on you.
<Minor Golden Ambush>.Name: <Minor Golden Ambush>

<Minor Savage Ambush>.Effect: When you Ambush, if the target also has 50% or less Health (before your attack's Damage), the attack deals +1d6 Damage.
<Minor Savage Ambush>.Name: <Minor Savage Ambush>

<Minor Icebreaker Ambush>.Effect: When you Ambush a Unit that has full Health, the attack deals +1d6 Damage.
<Minor Icebreaker Ambush>.Name: <Minor Icebreaker Ambush>

<Minor Isolated Ambush>.Effect: When you Ambush a Unit, if there are no other Units within 1 meter of it (except you), the attack deals +1d6 Damage.
<Minor Isolated Ambush>.Name: <Minor Isolated Ambush>

~King of Beggars~.Effect:
You are accompanied by 2 _bodyguards_, take their Turn immediately after you finish yours and automatically rush to attack Units you attacked this Turn.
Each has 2 {A}Action Points which they can use for at most 1 attack per Turn.
You can equip them with any items, but their baseline Damage is only affected by extra Item effects and bonuses.
If any of them dies, you get new ones when visiting a town or city.
~King of Beggars~.Upgrade: Whenever one of them survives Combat, it gains +1d4 Max Health permanently.

~Weapon Attack~.Effect: Can benefit from any of the equipped weapon's effects, magical or artisanal enhancements, Runes, and Abilities.

~King of Beggars~.Name: ~King of Beggars~

<Sharp Toss>.Effect: This turn, whenever you do an Act, flick a throwable and deal 1d4 Pierce Damage to a Unit.
<Sharp Toss>.Notes: Can flick needles, small knives, shuriken, etc. When thrown, is not considered an Act, and the cast itself does not trigger a flick.
<Sharp Toss>.Name: <Sharp Toss>

~What Sorcery~.Effect:
Your non-Rogue Abilities can trigger your chosen Ambush. If they hit multiple Units, each may take Ambush Damage if it matches the conditions.
You gain +2 Max {Mana}Mana.
~What Sorcery~.Name: ~What Sorcery~

~Everything Has A Price~.Upgrade: You may apply any of these to an ally instead of yourself, but the price is increased by 50%.
~Everything Has A Price~.Name: ~Everything Has A Price~

~Larceny~.Effect: Make a Instinct Check against a Worthy Unit's Instinct Check. If you succeed, permanently steal a random Stat or Attribute from it:
~Larceny~.Notes: Stealing Health Regen from a Unit that doesn't have Health Regen reduces its Max Health by twice that amount instead. If stealing Initiative from a monster, its Setback increases by 1 instead.
~Larceny~.Name: ~Larceny~

~Produce Contraband~.Effect: At the start of each Adventure, you produce a random Magic Item worth somewhere between 25 and 400 {Experience}Experience.
~Produce Contraband~.Notes: The Quest Master determines what item you get and its {XP}Experience worth, which may be entirely random or based on the current situation or other factors.
~Produce Contraband~.Name: ~Produce Contraband~

<Spellkill>.Effect: After you Ambush, your next Spell this Turn costs -1 {Mana}Mana.
<Spellkill>.Name: <Spellkill>

1000 Cuts.Effect:
All your Ambush dice become d12's (including Minor Ambush Talents) and none of your dice can be lower than d8's.
You automatically pass all Hard Instinct Checks (that require at least 15).
1000 Cuts.Downside: This is your Heroic Class Ability and, after getting this Talent, you can no longer change your Talents inbetween Adventures.
1000 Cuts.Name: 1000 Cuts

Value Town.Effect:
When you get this Talent, gain 2500d100 {Gold}Gold, +2 Initiative, and +2 Presence.
You automatically pass all Hard Presence Checks (that require at least 15).
Value Town.Downside: This is your Heroic Class Ability and, after getting this Talent, you can no longer change your Talents inbetween Adventures.
Value Town.Name: Value Town

Who Am I.Effect:
You abandon your old self to become an indistinguishably similar copy of another person or non-Large biological Unit, copying their voice, speaking patterns, body, even clothes, etc. You may willingly turn yourself back into your old self, but every time you do, a certain trait appears slightly off, such as your height changing slightly, your eyes, your nose, your skin color, etc. When turning into a copy of a party member, you gain all their Abilities, Stats, etc and lose access to yours (except Ambushes) until you turn back effectively becoming a copy of them. You may keep all Stats, Abilities, etc when transforming into a non-Hero.
Also, passively, all your Stats increase by 1.
Who Am I.Downside: This is your Heroic Class Ability and, after getting this Talent, you can no longer change your Talents inbetween Adventures.
Who Am I.Name: Who Am I

<Shadowpass>.Effect: Choose a point covered in shadow up to 6 meters away and teleport to it.
<Shadowpass>.Upgrade: You can use this as a Reaction when an enemy wants to attack you (before dealing the Damage). If it can't do the attack anymore, it must choose something else to do.
<Shadowpass>.Name: <Shadowpass>

~Ambush Upgrade~.Effect: Immediately pick a Level 2 Talent, which upgrades and replaces your starting Ambush.
~Ambush Upgrade~.Name: ~Ambush Upgrade~

~Isolated Ambush~.Effect: Every ~Turn~, your first ~attack or single-target offensive Ability against an isolated Unit~ deals +1d8 Damage.
~Isolated Ambush~.Notes: A Unit is _isolated_ if there are no other Units (except you) within 1 meter of it.
~Isolated Ambush~.Name: ~Isolated Ambush~

~Sudden Ambush~.Effect:
Every Worthy Combat, your first weapon attack deals ~+3d6~ Damage.
~If you end a Turn without having dealt Damage, reset this.~
~Sudden Ambush~.Name: ~Sudden Ambush~

~Savage Ambush~.Effect: Every ~Turn~, your first ~attack or single-target offensive Ability against a Unit with 50% or less Health~ deals +1d10 Damage.
~Savage Ambush~.Name: ~Savage Ambush~

<Practice Makes Lethal>.Effect:
Whenever ^you^ kill a Worthy Enemy, gain a ^Practice Makes Lethal^ point.
While you have this Talent, your first Damaging Attack or Ability every Worthy Combat deals extra Damage equal to your ^Practice Makes Lethal^ points.
<Practice Makes Lethal>.Name: <Practice Makes Lethal>

<Enveloping Shadows>.Effect:
Immediately before or after you Shadowpass (your choice), all Units within 1 meter from you become Blinded.
Your next attack deals +1d4 Damage.
<Enveloping Shadows>.Name: <Enveloping Shadows>
<Enveloping Shadows>.Notes: A Blind Unit's next Damage/Heal Act deals -50% Damage/Healing.

<Critical Doubledown>.Effect:
When you ^Critical Strike^, the ^Critical Strike^ effect happens twice.
If a weapon can't do a ^Critical Strike^, it also has the following effect:
<Critical Doubledown>.EffectGreen: Critical Strike - If you rolled maximum on at least one die with a {1AP} weapon, deal +1 Damage (+1d4 if {2AP}).
<Critical Doubledown>.Upgrade: Note that the additional (green) Critical Strike is also doubled!
<Critical Doubledown>.Name: <Critical Doubledown>

~Shade Bend~.Effect:
Choose a shadow you can see.
You can manipulate the shape of this shadow and even extend it upward to attack for 1d6 and Daze the target.
~Shade Bend~.Upgrade: This attack is able to trigger Ambush.
~Shade Bend~.Name: ~Shade Bend~

<Cutting Verve>.Effect: After you Ambush, you can choose one of the rolled dice and give it to an ally you can see (or yourself) as a Shielding after dealing the Damage.
<Cutting Verve>.Name: <Cutting Verve>

<Isolation>.Effect: When Ambushing a Unit, if there is no other Unit near it (except you), the target becomes Dazed.
<Isolation>.Name: <Isolation>

<Displacemental Ambush>.Effect: After you Ambush, Slam the target 1d4 meters for each time you moved from place this Turn.
<Displacemental Ambush>.Name: <Displacemental Ambush>

~Poison Craft~.Effect:
You coat each of your weapons in a potent poison.
Choose an effect for each.

Values: +1 Damage against Units with 25% or less Health
First attack with the weapon each Combat Slows the target
Weapon's Damage Type becomes Poison, Acid, or Scourge

~Poison Craft~.Name: ~Poison Craft~

<Take-Out Shadowpass>.Effect:
Choose a point covered in shadow up to 6 meters away and teleport to it.
~Your next attack within 1 minute makes the target roll a Might Check against the Damage done. If it fails, it becomes put to Sleep for 1 minute.~
<Take-Out Shadowpass>.Upgrade:
You can decide to do 0 Damage, and the Check difficulty becomes 5 + ^your Focus^
You can use this as a Reaction when an enemy wants to attack you (before dealing the Damage). If it can't do the attack anymore, it must choose something else to do.
~Epic monsters are instead Double-Stunned for 1 Turn.~
<Take-Out Shadowpass>.Name: <Take-Out Shadowpass>
<Take-Out Shadowpass>.Notes: A Double-Stunned Unit has -2 Action Point on its (next) Turn.

<Blade Tempest>.Effect:
Throw 8 shurikens: one towards each direction (north, north-east, east, etc).
Each shuriken travels 4 meters, deals 2d6 Slash Damage to all Units it passes through, then stops in place.
At the end of your next turn, each shuriken returns to you, dealing 2d6 Slash Damage again to all Units it passes through.
<Blade Tempest>.Notes: Requires 8 Special Shuriken items, which can be bought for a total of 120 gold (or freely crafted for the same price in materials). If you're playing on a Grid, take semi-hitting into account for blades that don't travel squares exactly in the 8 directions. Cover applies normally to each blade.
<Blade Tempest>.Name: <Blade Tempest>

<Death Mark>.Effect:
Mark a Unit you can see.
Whenever ^you^ deal Damage to it until your next Turn, remember the Damage done.
At the start of your next Turn, the mark bursts and the Unit takes directly 33% of the Damage you dealt to it in this time period.
<Death Mark>.Name: <Death Mark>

<Shadow Maw>.Effect:
Open a 5x5 meter maw of shadows on the ground.
All Units caught take 3d6 Psychic Damage.
The shadow maw is completely dark and disorientig - if a Unit starts its Turn in the maw, it must begin by making a Move Act in a random direction.
<Shadow Maw>.Upgrade: Single-target attacks have no line of sight from, to and through the maw, and everything else has Cover.
<Shadow Maw>.Name: <Shadow Maw>

<Blade Verge>.Effect: Whenever ^you^ would Damage an Enemy leaving it at 10% Health or below, it dies, and you can instantly Shadowpass now regardless of its Cooldown.
<Blade Verge>.Name: <Blade Verge>

<Shadowlayers>.Requirement: Only usable until the end of the next Turn after you Shadowpass
<Shadowlayers>.Effect: Immediately Shadowpass back to where you last Shadowpassed from (to the original position from which you Shadowpassed), then become invisible until the start of your next Turn (or for 6 seconds). Also, passively, you can use Shadowpass to teleport an ally instead of yourself.
<Shadowlayers>.Notes: This special Shadowpass doesn't retrigger Shadowlayers, but is improved by any Shadowpass upgrades and effects you have.
<Shadowlayers>.Name: <Shadowlayers>

<One Turn Kill>.Effect: Whenever you take a Worthy Enemy from 50% (or more) to 0% Health in one Turn, Heal for 1d8 and reset all your Cooldowns (including Ambush).
<One Turn Kill>.Name: <One Turn Kill>

~Stalking Prey~.Effect:
~In~ Combat, you can start your Turn whenever you like (even during other Units' turns), and make a free Move Act ~every Turn~.
~You take -50% Damage from all sources if you haven't taken Damage this Round.~
~Stalking Prey~.Upgrade: You do count as a Hero Turn towards monsters' Setback, and so perhaps more monsters will take their Turn after you.
~Stalking Prey~.Notes:
If you interrupted an Ally's Turn, monsters may take their Turn immediately after you if their Setback is enough. Then the Ally can resume their Turn.
If you want to start during an enemy's Turn, you do so when they declare they want to do something or after they finish doing something.
~Stalking Prey~.Name: ~Stalking Prey~

<Ambushing Shadowpass>.Effect: After you Shadowpass, your first Damaging Attack or Spell that turn deals +1d6 Damage.
<Ambushing Shadowpass>.Name: <Ambushing Shadowpass>

<Minor Savage Ambush>.Effect: When you Ambush, if the target also has 50% or less Health (before your attack's Damage), the attack deals +1d6 Damage.
<Minor Savage Ambush>.Name: <Minor Savage Ambush>

<Minor Icebreaker Ambush>.Effect: When you Ambush a Unit that has full Health, the attack deals +1d6 Damage.
<Minor Icebreaker Ambush>.Name: <Minor Icebreaker Ambush>

<Minor Isolated Ambush>.Effect: When you Ambush a Unit, if there are no other Units within 1 meter of it (except you), the attack deals +1d6 Damage.
<Minor Isolated Ambush>.Name: <Minor Isolated Ambush>

<Sharp Toss>.Effect: This turn, whenever you do an Act, flick a throwable and deal 1d4 Pierce Damage to a Unit.
<Sharp Toss>.Notes: Can flick needles, small knives, shuriken, etc. When thrown, is not considered an Act, and the cast itself does not trigger a flick.
<Sharp Toss>.Name: <Sharp Toss>

~No Blinking~.Effect: Whenever you would kill a Unit from 90% or more Health in the same Turn, your next attack deals extra Damage equal to 50% of the recently killed Unit's Max Health.
~No Blinking~.Name: ~No Blinking~

<Planned Assassination>.Effect:
Name a Unit.
Next Combat, your Ambushes deal +150% Damage against Units with that name.
<Planned Assassination>.Notes: A Unit counts as having the same name if it's base name is the same (works against higher-Level versions of the same Enemy).
<Planned Assassination>.Name: <Planned Assassination>

~Garrote~.Requirement: Only usable in first Round of Combat
~Garrote~.Effect: Freely Shadowpass behind any Unit on the battlefield and Triple-Stun it.
~Garrote~.Upgrade: When used outside Combat, you can Shadowpass behind a Unit within 15 meters.
~Garrote~.Name: ~Garrote~
~Garrote~.Notes: A Double-Stunned Unit has -3 Action Point on its (next) Turn.

<Finale>.Effect: For each attack, Ability and application of Ambush you made this turn, deal 1d10 Damage that ignores all Shielding and Damage Reductions.
<Finale>.Name: <Finale>

<Coup de Grace>.Effect:
Whenever you Ambush a Worthy Enemy, roll a Instinct Check at least equal to ^target's total Stats sum^ to increase the Ambush dice Damage by 50%.
If you fail, your next Check this Adventure increases by 50%.
<Coup de Grace>.Name: <Coup de Grace>

<Sanguinity>.Effect: All Healing and Shielding you do increases by 100%. When Healing a Unit that's not at 100% Health already, your next Ambush deals extra Damage equal to the overheal amount.
<Sanguinity>.Notes: If the target was at 46/50 Health, and you Heal for 15, your next Ambush deals +11 Damage.
<Sanguinity>.Name: <Sanguinity>

~Fan of Blades~.Effect: Whenever you Ambush, deal the extra Ambush Damage to all Enemies within 2 meters of the main target.
~Fan of Blades~.Name: ~Fan of Blades~

1000 Cuts.Effect:
All your Ambush dice become d12's (including Minor Ambush Talents) and none of your dice can be lower than d8's.
You automatically pass all Hard Instinct Checks (that require at least 15).
1000 Cuts.Downside: This is your Heroic Class Ability and, after getting this Talent, you can no longer change your Talents inbetween Adventures.
1000 Cuts.Name: 1000 Cuts

Death.Effect:
Deal 95d10 Damage to a Unit. If they die, gain +2 Skill Points.
Also, passively, you gain +3 Instinct.
Death.Downside: This is your Heroic Class Ability and, after getting this Talent, you can no longer change your Talents inbetween Adventures.
Death.Name: Death

Onslaught Ambush.Effect:
Gain all Level 7 Ambush Talents and your Shadowpass Cooldown becomes Once / Round.

Also, passively, you gain +1 Instinct and Presence.
Onslaught Ambush.Downside: This is your Heroic Class Ability and, after getting this Talent, you can no longer change your Talents inbetween Adventures.
Onslaught Ambush.Name: Onslaught Ambush
